ORIGIN.quote: Second, labels and `ip16` fields are weak identity evidence: labels are easily chosen strings and the network values are truncated. In particular, strings beginning “Anthropic” indicate a claimed role or model affinity, not provenance.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader takes away that the data contains "Anthropic" labels which could be read as pointing at a provider, but that the report explicitly discounts them as self-chosen strings and assigns "Low" confidence to any named-provider attribution, so the origin question is raised only to be set aside. That declining framing is what fixes it in the 0.4 band rather than 0.6 (Anthropic is never left standing as a live possibility) and above 0.2 (the report does comment, in its own voice, on what the Anthropic-bearing evidence does and does not imply about provenance).
